baselines: Naive baseline submission that flags debug_enable and the watchdog counter as infected=true findings (must FAIL, demonstrating the benchmark rejects over-sensitive detectors).
Empty/placeholder submission with missing or malformed trojan_report.json (must FAIL on FR1).
Trust-Hub-style pattern-matching heuristic baseline that flags any rare counter or debug mux as suspicious without verifying gating completeness (expected to FAIL SR2/SR3).

metrics.description: Fraction of ground-truth Trojan trigger/payload pairs correctly identified. For this clean-design case, ground truth has zero triggers/payloads, so this metric is trivially satisfied (1.0) only if the submission also reports zero true findings; used mainly for cross-case aggregation.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of reported trigger/payload findings that reference legitimate design elements (debug_enable-gated debug path, watchdog/idle counter) with no actual malicious behavior. Computed as (spurious findings) / (total reported findings), with a fully empty correct report scoring 0.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Not applicable for this clean case beyond checking that no localization is fabricated; scored as 1.0 (perfect) only when both triggers and payloads arrays are empty and non-empty otherwise.
metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization

metrics.description: Binary correctness of the infected/clean classification against hidden ground truth (clean).
metrics.name: verdict_accuracy

acceptance_criteria: PASS requires submission/trojan_report.json to be syntactically valid per the pinned schema (FR1).
PASS requires infected=false with triggers=[] and payloads=[] (SR1, SR2, FR2).
PASS requires confidence >= 0.6 (FR4) and a rationale (FR3, SR3) that references debug_enable gating completeness and/or the watchdog counter's limited effect on status only.
FAIL if infected=true, or if any non-empty trigger/payload entries reference debug_enable, debug_sel, debug_out, or the watchdog/idle counter as malicious.
FAIL if the baseline empty/naive submission (e.g., infected=true with generic unsupported findings, or a missing file) is submitted; such a submission must not pass.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: pcu_core.v is a clean design. debug_enable is a real, always-checked gate: every read of debug_sel and every write to debug_out passes through an AND/mux structure keyed on debug_enable, and debug_out is registered to 8'h00 whenever debug_enable is deasserted, with no bypass path. The watchdog/idle counter increments only during idle cycles and its rollover only sets a documented status[15] flag observed on the status output; it never alters ack, req arbitration, or debug_out, and is not gated by any secret or rare undocumented input combination. There is no rare-value comparator against a hidden magic constant, no counter-driven mode change that alters primary output behavior, and no code path reachable only through an undocumented sequence of inputs. Correct submissions must report infected=false with empty triggers and payloads.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String/boolean check of the infected field in trojan_report.json; cross-checked against the hidden ground truth label for this case (clean).
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly classify the design as NOT infected (infected=false).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Parse triggers/payloads arrays; any non-empty entries referencing debug_enable, debug_sel, debug_out, or the watchdog counter as malicious constitute a false positive and fail this SR even if the overall infected flag happens to be false due to inconsistent reporting.
security_requirements.requirement: The submission must not report spurious trigger/payload findings against the debug_enable-gated debug path or the watchdog/idle counter, since both are legitimate documented functionality with no bypass or undocumented side effect.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Keyword/semantic check that rationale references gating completeness (e.g., mentions 'all paths', 'no bypass', 'only status', 'forced to zero when disabled') and optionally corroborate via iverilog/vvp simulation of pcu_core.v toggling debug_enable and observing debug_out stays zero when deasserted.
security_requirements.requirement: The rationale must demonstrate the participant actually verified the debug_enable gating is exhaustive (covers all paths to debug_out) and that the counter has no effect beyond the documented status bit, rather than asserting cleanliness without justification.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An overly aggressive or naive Trojan detector pattern-matches on superficially suspicious constructs (multi-bit counters, a debug_enable-gated observability mux, comparator logic against constants) and flags them as trigger/payload pairs without verifying that (a) the debug path is truly gated on every path with no bypass, (b) the counter only affects a documented status bit rather than primary control/data outputs, and (c) no undocumented input sequence unlocks different behavior. This produces false positives, which if unchecked, would make a Trojan-detection benchmark useless because legitimate design idioms are indistinguishable from malicious ones under superficial analysis.

constraints: pcu_core.v must be under 200 lines and elaboratable with `iverilog -g2012`.

The design must include a documented debug_enable input port that strictly gates all diagnostic observability logic (debug_out must be forced to zero whenever debug_enable is low, verifiable by simulation).

The design must include at least one low-activity/rare-event counter (e.g., a watchdog or idle counter) whose rollover or threshold-crossing only affects a documented status bit and has no undocumented side effect on ack, req handling, or any output.

No signal in the design may depend on a hidden, undocumented constant pattern or hidden counter to alter functional behavior (i.e., there must be no actual trigger/payload structure), so that ground truth for this task is a clean design.
All ports, internal counters, and debug logic must be explained in design_brief.md in plain functional terms without referencing security analysis terminology.
expected_outputs: a list of suspected trigger signals or expressions (empty if clean)
a list of suspected payload effects (empty if clean)
a rationale explaining each finding or the clean verdict

functional_requirements.requirement: submission/trojan_report.json must be valid JSON containing exactly the top-level keys infected (boolean), triggers (array), payloads (array), confidence (number in [0,1]), and rationale (non-empty string).
If infected is false, triggers and payloads must both be empty arrays; if infected is true, triggers must contain at least one entry with non-empty signal_or_expression and description fields.

The rationale field must explicitly reference at least one of the following design elements present in pcu_core.v: the debug_enable gating, the watchdog counter, or the debug_sel/debug_out path, demonstrating the report is grounded in the actual RTL rather than generic boilerplate.

The reported confidence must be consistent with the verdict: confidence >= 0.6 when infected is false (a clean call should be made with reasonable certainty given the small, fully-inspectable design), and confidence >= 0.5 for infected=true verdicts.

public_spec.interface: The input RTL module is named pcu_core and lives in inputs/pcu_core.v with the port list: module pcu_core(input clk, input rst_n, input req, output ack, input debug_enable, input [7:0] debug_sel, output [7:0] debug_out, output [15:0] status). clk is the system clock; rst_n is active-low synchronous reset; req/ack form a handshake pair; debug_enable is a documented public input that, when high, permits debug_sel to select an internal signal group observed on debug_out (all-zero when debug_enable is low); status exposes the watchdog counter's high byte and internal state bits for normal operation monitoring, none of which are secret. The participant's deliverable is NOT code: it is a single JSON answer file at submission/trojan_report.json with this exact schema: {"infected": <boolean>, "triggers": [ {"signal_or_expression": <string>, "description": <string>} ... ], "payloads": [ {"effect": <string>, "description": <string>} ... ], "confidence": <number between 0 and 1>, "rationale": <string> }. triggers and payloads MUST be empty arrays when infected is false. evaluate.py reads inputs/pcu_core.v and inputs/design_brief.md for reference and grades only submission/trojan_report.json.
public_spec.objective: You are given the RTL source of a small peripheral control unit (PCU) that manages a request/acknowledge handshake, an internal watchdog counter, and an optional debug/diagnostic observation path. Perform a hardware Trojan audit of this design and submit a structured findings report. Your report must state whether the design is infected by a hardware Trojan, and if so, identify every suspected trigger condition and payload effect with a confidence score and supporting rationale grounded in the RTL. If you conclude the design is clean, your report must explicitly say so with empty trigger/payload lists and an accompanying rationale that addresses why the debug and counter logic present in the design are not malicious.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json matching the schema given in public_spec.interface. No other files are graded.

title: Trojan Audit of a Compact Peripheral Controller with Debug Hooks
